sections.html:
A cash buyer, an agent or a direct sale can all move fast here. The choice turns on repairs, timing and whether the buyer needs a loan. Ormond Beach is in Volusia County, and owners occupy 79.2% of its homes, so the typical seller is a homeowner and not a landlord.

  • Cash buyers skip the lender, which helps when a house has roof, flood or permit problems.
  • An agent listing reaches the widest pool of buyers. About 33.5% of residents are past 65, so expect many offers from retirees.
  • A direct sale saves the commission and leaves the contract, disclosures and recording to you.

First confirm that the property is inside city limits, because unincorporated Volusia County addresses follow different rules.

The city had an estimated 44,692 residents in July 2025, a 3.7% gain over the 2020 base.

Since 90.3% of residents stayed put over the past year, listings tend to come from long-term owners, and many of those houses carry decades of accumulated repairs. A buyer who pays cash and accepts the house as it stands saves such a seller from a repair list.

Lenders and insurers use FEMA flood maps to decide whether flood insurance is required. The city says every property lies in a flood zone of some kind. High-risk zones include A, AE, AO, V and VE. Zone X is a minimal-risk area that does not usually require flood insurance, although flooding can occur anywhere.

Before listing, look up your zone through the links on the city's floodplain pages and ask your insurance agent for a quote. A buyer's lender will ask for it, and a surprise on the quote can delay or end a closing. The Halifax River and part of the Tomoka River run through the city, which is why the question comes up so often.

sections.h2: Renting the house instead of selling
sections.html:
Long-term rental, meaning a lease over six months, is permitted in all residential districts. The city does not regulate it, so no business license is needed. Short-term rental, meaning transient lodging on a lease under six months, is not a permitted, conditional or special exception use in residential zoning districts.

The B-4, B-6 and B-7 commercial districts allow transient lodging, but those operators need a local business tax and must follow state lodging rules, with locations approved by the Site Plan Review Committee. A house in a residential district cannot be run as a vacation rental, and a buyer who hoped to do that will pay accordingly.

• Fences and driveways require permits, and the city asks for a survey showing the location.
  • Tree permits come from the Neighborhood Improvement Department at 386-229-7250.
  • A zoning confirmation letter costs $35 per address or parcel and is requested by email at comdev@ormondbeach.org.
  • A notice of commencement is required when work exceeds $5,000, or $7,500 for replacing an existing heating or air conditioning system, under section 713.13 of the Florida Statutes.
  • The Volusia County Property Appraiser's site shows your tax district: 201 is Ormond Beach and 200 is unincorporated northeast Volusia.

In 2014 the city also took jurisdiction over properties along North US Highway 1 from the Tomoka River bridge to the Volusia-Flagler County line, under an agreement with the county. If you own there, the district number tells you which government handles permits and code enforcement. Gather your permit records, survey and any zoning letter before you list, since title companies and buyers often request them.

sections.h2: Property taxes when the house sells
sections.html:
The Volusia County Property Appraiser values each parcel as of January 1. Bills reach owners in November, with early-payment discounts that shrink month by month. Exemption applications are due March 1, and unpaid bills turn delinquent on April 1.

Homestead can trim taxable value by up to $50,000, and Save Our Homes slows how quickly the assessment climbs. Many Ormond Beach owners stay for years, so the capped assessment can sit far below market value, and a sale ends that cushion for the buyer. If a prospective buyer asks what the bill will be, send them to the Volusia County Property Appraiser for an estimate.

sections.h2: Selling an inherited or family-transferred house
sections.html:
Florida has a streamlined summary administration for some smaller or older estates. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxable for deed stamps. A quitclaim deed is taxable, and it also counts as a change of ownership for assessment unless an exception applies.

A lady bird deed, also called an enhanced life estate deed, gets different treatment. A 2020 revenue advisement found that, on its facts, such a deed transferred no present beneficial interest and drew no stamp tax. The ruling is fact-specific, so have an attorney review your deed first. Under section 689.01, a conveyance of land must be written and signed before two witnesses.

Florida taxes the deed itself at $0.70 per $100 of consideration, and each party to it answers to the state whichever side the contract says will pay. The Volusia County clerk collects the tax at recording and adds recording fees that scale with page count. The closing agent can give you the exact total.

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens the file and searches the record for liens and unpaid taxes. If the house has open permits or an unrecorded owner change, that is when it surfaces. Sign the deed before witnesses as the statute requires, pay off any mortgage from the proceeds, and the clerk records the deed. With a cash buyer the sequence is the same, minus the lender's appraisal and underwriting.

Bring a photo ID, your deed or last closing paperwork, and the payoff statement if a mortgage remains. If the house is inside a flood zone, hand over the insurance declarations page so the buyer can compare it with their own quote. Tell the closing agent early about any open permit, tenant or estate paperwork, because each one adds a step and a delay if it comes out late.

faqs.q: Can I use my Ormond Beach house as a vacation rental?
faqs.a: Not in a residential zoning district. Short-term rental, defined as a lease under six months, is not a permitted, conditional or special exception use there. Leases longer than six months are allowed and need no city business license.

faqs.q: How do I tell if my address is in the City of Ormond Beach?
faqs.a: Search your address on the Volusia County Property Appraiser's site and read the tax district. District 201 is within Ormond Beach, while district 200 is unincorporated northeast Volusia and falls under county jurisdiction.

faqs.q: What does a zoning confirmation letter cost?
faqs.a: The city charges $35 per confirmation. Send the street address or tax parcel ID with the fee to comdev@ormondbeach.org. Buyers and title companies sometimes request one.

faqs.q: Is every house in Ormond Beach in a flood zone?
faqs.a: Yes, every property is in some FEMA flood zone. Zone X is a minimal-risk area that usually does not require flood insurance, while A, AE, AO, V and VE are high-risk. Your insurance agent can confirm what your lender will require.

faqs.q: Does my homestead exemption go to the buyer?
faqs.a: No. Yours ends when the house stops being your permanent residence, and the buyer applies by March 1 for a new one. The county reassesses at just value after the change of ownership.
